units.zh: 在位四年，奏尚書張林阿附侍中竇憲，而素行臧穢，又上洛陽令楊光，憲之賓客，在官貪殘，並不宜處位。
units.en: After four years in office he memorialized that Master of Writing Zhang Lin fawned on Dou Xian yet was corrupt by nature, and that Luoyang magistrate Yang Guang, a client of Dou Xian, was greedy and cruel in office—neither should hold rank.
units.literal: In office four years he memorialized that Master of Writing Zhang Lin fawned on attendant-in-ordinary Dou Xian yet his conduct was corrupt; he also reported Luoyang magistrate Yang Guang, a guest of Xian's, greedy and cruel in office—none were fit to hold position.

units.zh: 光報憲，憲奏弘大臣漏洩密事。
units.en: Yang Guang reported to Dou Xian, and Dou memorialized that Zheng Hong had leaked state secrets.
units.literal: Guang reported to Xian; Xian memorialized that Hong, a great minister, had leaked secret affairs.

units.zh: 帝詰讓弘，收上印綬。
units.en: The emperor rebuked Zheng Hong and took back his seal and cord.
units.literal: The emperor rebuked Hong and collected his seal and cord.

units.zh: 弘自詣廷尉，詔敕出之，因乞骸骨歸，未許。
units.en: Zheng Hong went to the commandant of justice himself; an edict ordered his release, but when he asked to retire he was not permitted.
units.literal: Hong himself went to the commandant of justice; an edict ordered his release; he then begged to return his bones home, but was not granted it.

units.zh: 病篤，上書陳謝，並言竇憲之短。
units.en: Gravely ill, he submitted a memorial of thanks and also reported Dou Xian's faults.
units.literal: Gravely ill, he submitted a memorial expressing thanks and also stating Dou Xian's faults.

units.zh: 帝省章，遣醫占弘病，比至已卒。
units.en: The emperor read the memorial and sent a physician to examine him; by the time the doctor arrived Zheng Hong was already dead.
units.literal: The emperor read the memorial and sent a physician to examine Hong's illness; by the time he arrived Hong had already died.

units.zh: 臨歿悉還賜物，敕妻子褐巾布衣素棺殯殮，以還鄉里。
units.en: On his deathbed he returned all imperial gifts and ordered his wife and children to bury him in plain cloth and a plain coffin, then return home.
units.literal: At death he returned all granted goods; he ordered his wife and children to wear brown headcloths and plain clothes and a plain coffin for burial, then return to their home district.

units.zh: 周章字次叔，南陽隨人也。
units.en: Zhou Zhang, styled Cishu, came from Sui in Nanyang commandery.
units.literal: Zhou Zhang, courtesy name Cishu, was a man of Sui in Nanyang.

units.zh: 初仕郡為功曹。
units.en: He first served the commandery as merit assessor.
units.literal: At first he served the commandery as merit assessor.

units.zh: 時大將軍竇憲免，封冠軍侯就國。
units.en: When Grand General Dou Xian was dismissed and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun, he returned to his fief.
units.literal: At that time Grand General Dou Xian was dismissed and enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanjun, returning to his state.

units.zh: 章從太守行春到冠軍，太守猶欲謁之。
units.en: Zhou Zhang accompanied the governor on a spring inspection tour to Guanjun; the governor still meant to call on Dou Xian.
units.literal: Zhang followed the governor on the spring circuit to Guanjun; the governor still wished to call on Xian.

units.zh: 章進諫曰：『今日公行春，豈可越儀私交。
units.en: Zhou Zhang remonstrated: "Today you are on the spring circuit—how can you overstep protocol for a private visit?
units.literal: Zhang advanced remonstrance saying: "Today Your Excellency is on the spring circuit—how can you overstep ritual for a private visit?

units.zh: 且憲椒房之親，勢傾王室，而退就藩國，禍福難量。
units.en: Moreover Dou Xian is empress kin whose power once tilted the throne; now he withdraws to his fief—fortune and disaster are hard to measure.
units.literal: Moreover Xian is kin of the empress's chamber; his power once tilted the royal house; now he withdraws to his feudal state—fortune and disaster are hard to measure.

units.zh: 明府剖符大臣，千里重任，舉止進退，其可輕乎？』
units.en: You are a minister bearing the imperial tally, charged with a thousand li—can your comings and goings be treated lightly?"
units.literal: Your Excellency is a minister bearing the split tally, charged with a thousand li—can your comings and goings be treated lightly?"

units.zh: 太守不聽，遂便升車。
units.en: The governor would not listen and mounted his carriage.
units.literal: The governor would not listen and then mounted his carriage.

units.zh: 章前拔佩刀絕馬鞅，於是乃止。
units.en: Zhou Zhang stepped forward, drew his sword, and cut the horse's traces—only then did the governor stop.
units.literal: Zhang stepped forward, drew his girdle sword, and cut the horse's traces; only then did he stop.

units.zh: 及憲被誅，公卿以下多以交關得罪，太守幸免，以此重章。
units.en: When Dou Xian was executed, grandees and officials were punished for association; the governor escaped by luck and thereafter held Zhou Zhang in high esteem.
units.literal: When Xian was executed, grandees and officials below mostly were punished for association; the governor escaped by luck, and for this held Zhang in high esteem.

units.zh: 舉孝廉，六遷為五官中郎將。
units.en: Nominated filial and incorrupt, he rose through six promotions to colonel of the Five Offices.
units.literal: Raised filial and incorrupt, through six transfers he became colonel of the Five Offices.

units.zh: 延平元年，為光祿勳。
units.en: In Yanping 1 he became Minister of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: In the first year of Yanping he became Minister of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 永初元年，代魏霸為太常。
units.en: In Yongchu 1 he succeeded Wei Ba as Minister of Ceremonies.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongchu he replaced Wei Ba as Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 其冬，代尹勤為司空。
units.en: That winter he succeeded Yin Qin as Minister of Works.
units.literal: That winter he replaced Yin Qin as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 是時中常侍鄭眾，蔡倫等皆秉勢豫政，章數進直言。
units.en: Palace attendants Zheng Zhong, Cai Lun, and others then held power in government; Zhou Zhang repeatedly offered blunt counsel.
units.literal: At this time the palace attendants Zheng Zhong, Cai Lun, and others all held power and took part in government; Zhang repeatedly advanced blunt counsel.

units.zh: 初，和帝崩，鄧太后以皇子勝有痼疾，不可奉承宗廟，貪殤帝孩抱，養為己子，故立之，以勝為平原王。
units.en: When Emperor He died, Empress Dowager Deng held that Prince Sheng had a chronic illness and could not attend the ancestral temple; she seized the infant Emperor Shang, raised him as her own, enthroned him, and made Sheng King of Pingyuan.
units.literal: At first, when Emperor He died, Empress Dowager Deng held that the prince Sheng had chronic illness and could not attend the ancestral temple; coveting the infant Emperor Shang in her arms, she raised him as her own son and therefore enthroned him, making Sheng King of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 及殤帝崩，群臣以勝疾非痼、意咸歸之，太后以前既不立，恐後為怨，乃立和帝兄清河孝王子祐，是為安帝。
units.en: When Emperor Shang died, ministers held that Sheng's illness was not chronic and hearts turned to him; fearing later resentment for not having enthroned him earlier, the empress dowager enthroned Liu You, son of King Xiao of Qinghe and brother of Emperor He—Emperor An.
units.literal: When Emperor Shang died, the host of ministers held that Sheng's illness was not chronic and their hearts all turned to him; the empress dowager, because she had not enthroned him before, feared later resentment, and therefore enthroned You, son of King Xiao of Qinghe, brother of Emperor He—this was Emperor An.

units.zh: 章以眾心不附，遂密謀閉宮門，誅車騎將軍鄧騭兄弟及鄭眾、蔡倫，劫尚書，廢太后於南宮，封帝為遠國王，而立平原王勝。
units.en: Zhou Zhang, finding popular hearts unattached, secretly plotted to shut the palace gates, execute Deng Zhi and his brothers along with Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun, seize the Masters of Writing, depose the empress dowager in the Southern Palace, banish the emperor to a distant kingdom, and enthrone Prince Sheng of Pingyuan.
units.literal: Zhang, because popular hearts did not attach, then secretly plotted to shut the palace gates, execute Chariots-and-Cavalry General Deng Zhi and his brothers along with Zheng Zhong and Cai Lun, seize the Masters of Writing, depose the empress dowager in the Southern Palace, enfeoff the emperor as king of a distant state, and enthrone King of Pingyuan Sheng.

units.zh: 事覺，策免，章自殺。
units.en: The plot was discovered; he was dismissed by edict and killed himself.
units.literal: The plot was discovered; he was dismissed by edict; Zhang killed himself.

units.zh: 家無餘財，諸子易衣而出，並日而食。
units.en: The household had no surplus wealth; his sons exchanged clothes to go out and ate on alternate days.
units.literal: The household had no surplus wealth; his sons exchanged clothes to go out and ate on alternate days.

units.zh: 論曰：孔子稱『可與立，未可與權』。
units.en: The historian remarks: Confucius said, 'You can stand firm with some men—not weigh shifting circumstances with every one.'
units.literal: The appraisal says: Confucius called 'May stand with him, not yet may weigh circumstances with him.'

units.zh: 權也者，反常者也。
units.en: Expediency means departing from the usual rule.
units.literal: Weighing circumstances is departing from the norm.

units.zh: 將從反常之事，必資非常之會，使夫舉無違妄，誌行名全。
units.en: Acting outside the norm calls for extraordinary timing—only then can the deed avoid folly and leave ambition, deed, and reputation intact.
units.literal: About to follow abnormal affairs, must rely on extraordinary conjunctions, causing those undertakings without violation or recklessness, aspiration and conduct name preserved whole.

units.zh: 周章身非負圖之托，德乏萬夫之望，主無絕天之釁，
units.en: Zhou Zhang bore no Duke-of-Zhou mandate; he lacked popular esteem; the emperor gave Heaven no cause for revolt,
units.literal: Zhou Zhang bore no regent's charge like the Duke of Zhou; virtue fell short of the multitude's hopes; the ruler showed no crime against Heaven's mandate,

units.zh: 地有既安之埶，而創慮於難圖，希功於理絕，不已悖乎！
units.en: the realm already rested secure—yet he plotted the impossible and hoped for success where cause was dead—was that not folly?
units.literal: earth had already settled posture, yet he devised schemes on hard-to-plan matters, hoped achievement where principle was cut off—is it not already perverse!

units.zh: 如令君器易以下議，即鬥筲必能叨天業，狂夫豎臣亦自奮矣。
units.en: If high office bends to petty counsel, every small talent will grasp at the Mandate and cranks will rush forward.
units.literal: If high office yields easily to counsel from below, then petty measure could seize heaven's enterprise; madmen and petty ministers too would exert themselves.

units.zh: 孟軻有言曰：『有伊尹之心則可，無伊尹之心則篡矣。』
units.en: Mencius said, 'With Yi Yin's intent it is permissible; without it, it is usurpation.'
units.literal: Meng Ke had words saying: 'Having Yi Yin's heart then acceptable; lacking Yi Yin's heart then usurpation.'

units.zh: 於戲，方來之人戒之哉！
units.en: Alas—let those who come after take warning!
units.literal: Alas, those who come after—guard against it!

units.zh: 贊曰：朱定北州，激成寵尤。
units.en: Verse says: Zhu Fu steadied Youzhou but baited Peng Chong into rebellion.
units.literal: The encomium says: Zhu settled northern province; incited completion Chong's fault.

units.zh: 魴用降帑，延感歸囚。
units.en: Feng Fang drew grain from the treasury to win surrender; Yu Yan's grace sent prisoners home on time.
units.literal: Fang used surrendering treasury; Yan moved returning prisoners.

units.zh: 鄭、竇怨偶，代相為仇，周章反道，小智大謀。
units.en: Zheng Hong and the Dou clan were paired in strife; generation after generation turned hostile; Zhou Zhang defied the Way—petty wit, vaulting plot.
units.literal: Zheng, Dou paired enmity; generation succeeding became foes; Zhou Zhang opposed the Way; small wisdom great plotting.

units.zh: 以河南尹範遷有清行，代為司徒。
units.en: Fan Qian of Henan, noted for clean living, was named minister of education in his place.
units.literal: Because Fan Qian, metropolitan governor of Henan, had pure conduct, he replaced him as Minister of Education.

units.zh: 遷字子廬，沛國人，初為漁陽太守，以智略安邊，匈奴不敢入界。
units.en: Fan Qian, styled Zilu, came from the princedom of Pei. As grand administrator of Yuyang he secured the frontier by shrewd policy, and the Xiongnu would not cross his border.
units.literal: Qian, courtesy name Zilu, was a man of the Principality of Pei; at first he was grand administrator of Yuyang, and by strategy and planning he pacified the border, so the Xiongnu did not dare enter his territory.

units.zh: 遷曰：『吾備位大臣而蓄財求利，何以示後世！』
units.en: Fan Qian replied, 'I sit among the great ministers; if I piled up silver for my heirs, what example would I leave!'
units.literal: Qian said, 'I occupy a minister's place yet hoard wealth and seek profit—how would I show posterity!'

units.zh: 及在公輔，有宅數畝，田不過一頃，復推與兄子。
units.en: Even as one of the chief ministers he owned only a few mu of house and less than one qing of land, which he then signed over to his nephew.
units.literal: When among the highest ministers, he had a residence of several mu and fields not exceeding one qing, yet again he pushed them to his elder brother's son.

units.zh: 五年，卒於家，時年八十七。
units.en: He died at home in the fifth year, at the age of eighty-seven.
units.literal: In the fifth year, he died at home, aged eighty-seven.

units.zh: 在位四年薨，家無擔石焉。
units.en: He died in office after four years, leaving his household without a peck to spare.
units.literal: After four years in office he died; the family had not a dan or shi of grain.

units.zh: 其妻嘗謂曰：『君有四子而無立錐之地，可余奉祿，以為後世業。』
units.en: His wife once said, 'You have four sons and not a handspan of soil—why not salt away your salary for their future.'
units.literal: His wife once said to him, 'You have four sons yet not land to stick an awl; you could set aside your salary to build an estate for posterity.'

units.zh: 時隗囂據壟擁眾，招輯英俊，而公孫述稱帝於蜀漢，天下雲擾，大者連州郡，小者據縣邑。
units.en: Wei Xiao then blocked the Long road and recruited talent while Gongsun Shu styled himself emperor in Shu; the realm splintered into rival zones large and small.
units.literal: At that time Wei Xiao held Long and gathered heroes, while Gongsun Shu declared himself emperor in Shu-Han; all under Heaven boiled like a cloud; the great linked commanderies and the small seized counties.

units.zh: 囂問彪曰：「往者周亡，戰國並爭，天下分裂，數世然後乃定，其抑者從橫之事復起於今乎？
units.en: Wei Xiao asked Ban Biao, "In former times when Zhou fell, the Warring States strove together and the realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled—will the affairs of vertical and horizontal alliances rise again now,
units.literal: Xiao asked Biao, "In former times when Zhou fell, the Warring States strove together, the realm split apart, and only after several generations was it settled—will the affairs of vertical and horizontal alliances rise again now?

units.zh: 囂曰：「先生言周、漢之勢，可也，至於但見愚民習識劉氏姓號之故，而謂漢家復興，疏矣！
units.en: Wei Xiao said, "What you say, sir, about the tendencies of Zhou and Han is acceptable, but to infer from the mere fact that foolish commoners are habituated to the Liu surname that the house of Han will rise again is far too loose!
units.literal: Xiao said, "What you say, sir, about the tendencies of Zhou and Han is acceptable, but to infer from the mere fact that foolish commoners are habituated to the Liu surname that the house of Han will rise again is far too loose!

units.zh: 既感囂言，又愍狂狡之不息，乃著王命論以救時難。
units.en: Half persuaded by Wei Xiao yet sick of endless adventurism, Ban Biao drafted the Discourse on the King's Mandate to steady a chaotic age.
units.literal: Having been moved by Xiao's words and also pitying that wild cunning would not cease, he thereupon composed the Discourse on the King's Mandate to rescue the troubles of the age.

units.zh: 將承運迭興在於一人也？
units.en: or will the received mandate pass in turn and concentrate in a single man?
units.literal: Or will the received mandate pass in turn and concentrate in a single man?

units.zh: 願先生論之。」
units.en: He begged Ban Biao to give his reading."
units.literal: I beg the master to discuss it."

units.zh: 昔秦失其鹿，劉季逐而掎之，時民復知漢虖！」
units.en: In olden times Qin lost the deer, and Liu Ji chased and seized it—did the people then even know there would be a Han?"
units.literal: In olden times Qin lost the deer, and Liu Ji chased and seized it—did the people then even know there would be a Han?"

units.zh: 存節武鷙慷慨，有大節，野戰壁守，皆其所長，威名聞於境外，深為末帝所重，而木強忠厚，有賈復之風焉。
units.en: Fierce, generous, and resolute, he excelled in the field and behind walls; his fame reached beyond the border and the Last Emperor prized him, yet he was bluntly honest in the manner of Jia Fu.
units.literal: Cunjie was martially fierce and generously spirited, with great integrity; field battle and wall defense were alike his strengths; his martial fame was heard beyond the borders; the Last Emperor valued him deeply, yet he was stubbornly honest and loyal, having the manner of Jia Fu.

units.zh: 永平中，車駕近出，而信陽侯陰就幹突禁衛，車府令徐匡鉤就車，收禦者送獄。
units.en: During Yongping the emperor rode out on a short tour; Marquis Yin Jiu of Xinyang forced his way through the palace guard; carriage-house director Xu Kuang seized his chariot and jailed the charioteer.
units.literal: In the Yongping period, the imperial carriage went out on a near excursion, and Marquis of Xinyang Yin Jiu burst through the forbidden guard; the carriage-house director Xu Kuang hooked Jiu's carriage and arrested the driver and sent him to prison.

units.zh: 良上言曰：『信陽侯就倚恃外戚，幹犯乘輿，無人臣禮，為大不敬。
units.en: Wu Liang memorialized: 'Yin Jiu trades on his status as an imperial in-law, obstructs the imperial train, and shows none of a subject's deference—that is grave disrespect.'
units.literal: Liang submitted words, saying, 'Marquis of Xinyang Jiu relies on being maternal kin, violates the imperial equipage, lacks the ritual of minister and subject, and is greatly irreverent.'

units.zh: 而王次兄仲於代。
units.en: His second brother, Zhong, was made King of Dai.
units.literal: He then established his second brother Zhong as king in Dai.

units.zh: 楚元王劉交者，高祖之同母少弟也，字游。
units.en: Liu Jiao, King Yuan of Chu, was the youngest brother of Emperor Gaozu by the same mother, and bore the courtesy name You.
units.literal: King Yuan of Chu, Liu Jiao, was Gaozu's younger brother by the same mother, styled You.

units.zh: 太上皇以為言，高祖曰：「某非忘封之也，為其母不長者耳。」
units.en: The Retired Emperor raised the matter, and Gaozu replied, "It is not that I forgot to grant him a fief—it is because his mother was no woman of virtue."
units.literal: The Supreme Emperor spoke of this, and Gaozu said, "It is not that I forgot to enfeoff him; it is because his mother was not virtuous."

units.zh: 遷，故車騎將軍單超之弟，中官相黨，遂共誹章誣緄，坐與司隸校尉李膺、大司農劉祐俱輸左校。
units.en: Shan Qian was the younger brother of the late General Shan Chao; the eunuchs closed ranks and framed Feng Gun. He was sentenced to hard labor at the Left Craftsmen prison alongside Li Ying and Liu You.
units.literal: Qian was the younger brother of the former General of Chariots and Cavalry Shan Chao; the palace officials formed a faction and together slandered with memorials and falsely accused Gun; by crime together with Colonel Director of Retainers Li Ying and Minister of Finance Liu You all were sent to the Left Craftsmen.

units.zh: 太尉趙憙慕其誌，每歲時遣子問以酒糧，皆辭不受。
units.en: Grand Commandant Zhao Xi admired his integrity and sent seasonal gifts of wine and grain through his son; Gong courteously refused every time.
units.literal: Grand Commandant Zhao Xi admired his intent; every season he sent his son with gifts of wine and grain; all were declined and not accepted.

units.zh: 太傅趙憙聞而辟之。
units.en: Grand Tutor Zhao Xi heard of him and brought him onto his staff.
units.literal: Grand Tutor Zhao Xi heard of it and summoned him.

units.zh: 憙復舉恭直言，特詔公車，拜中牟令。
units.en: Zhao Xi next recommended him for forthright counsel; an edict routed him through the Waiting Coaches office and named him magistrate of Zhongmou.
units.literal: Xi again recommended Gong for blunt counsel; he was specially summoned by edict to the Waiting Coaches office and appointed magistrate of Zhongmou.

units.zh: 季文子妾不衣帛，魯人以為美談。
units.en: Ji Wenzi's concubines wore no silk; the people of Lu praised it as a noble example.
units.literal: Ji Wenzi's concubines did not wear silk; the people of Lu took it as a fine tale.

units.zh: 東都中興，萌、寵違戾。
units.en: when the Eastern Capital rose again, Yin and Chong broke faith.
units.literal: when the Eastern Capital revived, Yin and Chong defied allegiance.

units.zh: 太守第五倫擢為督郵。
units.en: Governor Diwu Lun raised him to supervising clerk.
units.literal: Governor Diwu Lun promoted him to supervising clerk.

units.zh: 及倫作司徒，令班固為文薦夷吾曰：
units.en: When Diwu Lun became minister of education he told Ban Gu to draft a memorial praising Xie Yiwu:
units.literal: When Lun became minister of education, he ordered Ban Gu to compose a text recommending Yiwu, saying,

units.zh: 臣聞堯登稷、契，政隆太平；
units.en: Your servant has heard that when Yao raised Ji and Xie, peace spread across the realm;
units.literal: Your servant has heard that when Yao elevated Ji and Xie, government flourished into great peace;

units.zh: 舜用皋陶，政致雍熙、殷、周雖有高宗、昌、發之君，猶賴傅說、呂望之策，故能克崇其業，允協大中。
units.en: Shun used Gao Yao and harmony followed. Yin and Zhou boasted kings like Gaozong, Wen, and Wu, yet even they leaned on Fu Yue and Lü Wang—only thus could they magnify their work and hit the great mean.
units.literal: Shun employed Gao Yao and government reached perfect harmony; although Yin and Zhou had sovereigns such as Gaozong, Chang, and Fa, they still relied on the plans of Fu Yue and Lü Wang, and therefore were able to exalt their enterprises and truly accord with the great mean.

units.zh: 竊見鉅鹿太守會稽謝夷吾，出自東州，厥土塗泥，而英姿挺特，奇偉秀出。
units.en: Your servant has watched Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he springs from the eastern mudflats, his mien is heroic, his talent towering.
units.literal: Your servant has privately observed Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he comes from the eastern regions where the soil is mud and mire, his heroic bearing stands apart, strange and grand, outstanding among his peers.

units.zh: 願乞骸骨，更授夷吾，上以光七曜之明，下以厭率土之望，庶令微臣塞咎免悔。
units.en: Let me yield my bones and yield the post to Yiwu—above to light the seven governors, below to quiet the empire—so this fool may dodge blame and regret.
units.literal: I beg to surrender my bones and in turn appoint Yiwu—above to brighten the seven luminaries, below to satisfy the hopes of all within the seas—so that perhaps your humble servant may block fault and escape regret.

units.zh: 時，烏程長有臧釁，倫使收案其罪。
units.en: The magistrate of Wucheng was rumored corrupt; Diwu Lun ordered Xie Yiwu to arrest and examine him.
units.literal: At the time the magistrate of Wucheng bore a taint of corruption; Lun sent Yiwu to seize him and investigate his crimes.

units.zh: 及還，白倫曰：「竊以佔候，知長當死。
units.en: Back at headquarters he told Diwu Lun, 'My divination shows the magistrate is dying.
units.literal: When he returned he reported to Lun, saying, 'Your servant has privately divined by omens and knows the magistrate is about to die.

units.zh: 倫聽其言，至月餘，果有驛馬齎長印綬，上言暴卒。
units.en: Diwu Lun waited; a month later couriers arrived with the dead man's seal and word of a sudden death.
units.literal: Lun listened to his words, and after a little more than a month, indeed relay horses brought the magistrate's seal and ribbon with a report that he had died suddenly.

units.zh: 倫以此益禮信之。
units.en: From then on Diwu Lun honored him the more.
units.literal: Lun for this reason treated him with still greater courtesy and trust.

units.zh: 闡弘道奧，同史蘇、京房之倫。
units.en: in opening the Way's depths he ranks with Shi Su and Jing Fang.
units.literal: expounding the profound of the Way, he is of the same class as Shi Su and Jing Fang.

units.zh: 方之古賢，實有倫序；
units.en: Set beside the ancients he holds his rank;
units.literal: Compared with the worthies of antiquity, he truly has his proper ordering;

units.zh: 延平元年，代尹勤為太常。
units.en: In Yanping 1 he succeeded Yin Qin as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
units.literal: In the first year of Yanping he replaced Yin Qin as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 和帝即位，太傅邓彪奏䊸在任过酷，不宜典司京辇。
units.en: At Emperor He’s accession, Grand Tutor Deng Biao argued that Zhou Xu’s tenure had been too bloody for him to police the capital region.
units.literal: When Emperor He ascended the throne, Grand Tutor Deng Biao memorialized that Xu in office had been excessively cruel and was unsuited to oversee the capital precincts.

units.zh: 靈帝初，征拜太中大夫，傳講華光殿。
units.en: Early in Emperor Ling's reign he became Grand Counselor of the Palace and lectured on the classics at Huaguang Hall.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ling he was summoned and appointed Grand Counselor of the Palace; lectured by transmission at Huaguang Hall.

units.zh: 靈帝頗好學藝，每引見寬，常令講經。
units.en: Emperor Ling loved scholarship and often summoned Liu Kuan to expound the canon.
units.literal: Emperor Ling rather liked learning and arts; whenever summoning audience with Kuan he regularly ordered him to expound the classics.

units.zh: 帝問：『太尉醉邪？』
units.en: The emperor asked whether the Grand Commandant was drunk.
units.literal: The emperor asked, "Is the Grand Commandant drunk?"

units.zh: 帝重其言。
units.en: The emperor respected his candor.
units.literal: The emperor valued his words.

units.zh: 熹平五年，代許訓為太尉。
units.en: In Xiping 5 he succeeded Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xiping he replaced Xu Xun as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 類田文之愛客，同鄭莊之好賢。
units.en: Like Lord Mengchang he loved guests; like Zheng Zhuang he delighted in the worthy.
units.literal: Like Lord Mengchang he loved guests, like Zheng Zhuang he delighted in the worthy.

units.zh: 子鯈嗣。
units.en: His son Fan Tiao inherited the title.
units.literal: His son Tiao succeeded.

units.zh: 鯈字長魚，謹約有父風。
units.en: Fan Tiao, courtesy name Changyu, was as careful and restrained as his father.
units.literal: Tiao, courtesy name Changyu, was cautious and restrained and had his father's manner.

units.zh: 二年，以壽張國益東平王，徙封鯈燕侯。
units.en: In the second year the state of Shouzhang was added to the Prince of Dongping, and Fan Tiao was transferred to marquis of Yan.
units.literal: In the second year, the state of Shouzhang was added to the Prince of Dongping, and Tiao was transferred to marquis of Yan.

units.zh: 十年，鯈卒，赗贈甚厚，謚曰哀侯。
units.en: In the tenth year of Yongping he died with rich funeral honors and the posthumous title Pitiful Marquis.
units.literal: In the tenth year, Tiao died; burial gifts were very generous; posthumous title was marquis of pity.

units.zh: 初，鯈刪定《公羊嚴氏春秋》章句，世號『樊侯學』，教授門徒前後三千餘人。
units.en: Fan Tiao had edited the Yan school Gongyang commentary; the age called it Marquis Fan's school, and he taught more than three thousand students.
units.literal: Earlier, Tiao edited and fixed the Gongyang Yan lineage Spring and Autumn Annals sentence sections; the age titled it 'marquis of Fan learning'; he taught disciples before and after over three thousand persons.

units.zh: 帝崩，鯈為復土校尉。
units.en: When the emperor died, Fan Tiao served as colonel in charge of the imperial burial.
units.literal: When the emperor died, Tiao became colonel of the earth-returning [burial].

units.zh: 永平元年，拜長水校尉，與公卿雜定郊祠禮儀，以讖記正《五經》異說。
units.en: In Yongping 1 he was appointed Colonel of the Chang River and, with the high ministers, jointly settled suburban sacrifice ritual, using prognostic texts to correct variant readings in the Five Classics.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongping he was appointed Colonel of the Chang River and, with the high ministers, jointly settled suburban sacrifice ritual, using prognostic texts to correct variant readings in the Five Classics.

units.zh: 服闋，就侍中丁恭受《公羊嚴氏春秋》。
units.en: After mourning he studied the Yan school Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals under Attendant-in-Chief Ding Gong.
units.literal: When mourning was complete, he went to attendant Ding Gong to receive the Gongyang Yan lineage Spring and Autumn Annals.

units.zh: 明年，賜鯈弟鮪及從昆弟七人合錢五千萬。
units.en: The following year the court gave Fan Wei and seven cousins fifty million cash.
units.literal: The next year, he granted Tiao's younger brother Wei and seven cousins-brother in all fifty million cash.

units.zh: 弟子潁川李脩、九江夏勤，皆為三公。
units.en: His pupils Li Xiu of Yingchuan and Xia Qin of Jiujiang rose to the three dukes.
units.literal: Disciples Li Xiu of Yingchuan and Xia Qin of Jiujiang both became three dukes.

units.zh: 北海周澤、瑯邪承宮並海內大儒，鯈皆以為師友而致之於朝。
units.en: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both leading scholars of the realm; Fan Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.
units.literal: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both great Confucian scholars within the realm; Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.

units.zh: 事後母至孝，及母卒，哀思過禮，毀病不自支，世祖常遣中黃門朝暮送饘粥。
units.en: He mourned his stepmother past the bounds of ritual until he fell ill; Emperor Guangwu sent eunuchs morning and evening with gruel.
units.literal: He served his stepmother with utmost filiality; when she died, grief and longing exceeded the rites; he wasted away ill and could not support himself; Shizu often sent palace attendants morning and evening to deliver gruel.

units.zh: 長子汜嗣，以次子郴、梵為郎。
units.en: The eldest son Fan Si inherited; younger sons Chen and Fan became gentlemen of the palace.
units.literal: The eldest son Si succeeded; the second sons Chen and Fan were made gentlemen.

units.zh: 建武中，禁網尚闊，諸王既長，各招引賓客，以鯈外戚，爭遣致之，而鯈清靜自保，無所交結。
units.en: In Jianwu the laws were loose; grown princes vied for clients and courted Fan Tiao as imperial in-law, but he kept to himself and joined no faction.
units.literal: In the Jianwu period, the prohibition net was still loose; the various princes having grown, each summoned and drew retainers; because Tiao was outer kin, they vied to send and bring him, yet Tiao was clear and quiet, preserving himself, associating and connecting with none.

units.zh: 上言郡國舉孝廉，率取年少能報恩者，耆宿大賢多見廢棄，宜敕郡國簡用良俊。
units.en: He memorialized that commanderies and kingdoms recommending Filial and Incorrupt candidates favored the young who could repay favors, while elderly worthies were often passed over, and urged that they select truly outstanding men.
units.literal: He memorialized that when commanderies and kingdoms recommended Filial and Incorrupt candidates, they consistently took the young who could repay favors, while elderly great worthies were mostly cast aside—commanderies and kingdoms should be ordered to select good outstanding men.

units.zh: 又議刑辟宜須秋月，以順時氣。
units.en: He also argued that capital punishments should await the autumn month, in accord with seasonal qi.
units.literal: He also argued that capital punishments should await the autumn month, to accord with seasonal qi.

units.zh: 鯈仰而對曰：『天下高帝天下，非陛下之天下也。
units.en: Fan Tiao looked up and replied: 'The realm is Emperor Gao's realm, not Your Majesty's realm alone.
units.literal: Tiao looked up and replied: 'The realm is Gao Di's realm, not Your Majesty's realm alone.

units.zh: 《春秋》之義。
units.en: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals:
units.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals:

units.zh: 「君親無將，將而誅焉」。
units.en: "For lord and parent there must be no rebellious intent—one who rebels shall be executed."
units.literal: "For lord and parent there must be no rebellious intent—one who rebels shall be executed."

units.zh: 是以周公誅弟，季友鴆兄，經傳大之。
units.en: Therefore the Duke of Zhou executed his younger brother and Ji You poisoned his elder brother—the classics and commentaries greatly praise this.
units.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou executed his younger brother, and Ji You poisoned his elder brother—the classics and commentaries greatly praise this.

units.zh: 臣等以荊屬託母弟，陛下留聖心，加惻隱，故敢請耳。
units.en: We thought that because Jing is the empress-dowager's younger brother, Your Majesty would retain sage consideration and show compassion—therefore we dared only to petition.
units.literal: We, your servants, because Jing is the empress-dowager's younger brother, thought Your Majesty would retain sage consideration and add compassion—therefore we dared only to petition.

units.zh: 如令陛下子，臣等專誅而已。』
units.en: Had he been Your Majesty's son, we would have executed him outright.'
units.literal: Had he been Your Majesty's son, we would have executed him outright.'

units.zh: 其後弟鮪為子賞求楚王英女敬鄉公主，鯈聞而止之，曰：『建武時，吾家並受榮寵，一宗五侯。
units.en: Later his younger brother Wei sought for his son Shang the Princess Jingxiang, daughter of Prince Ying of Chu; Fan Tiao heard of it and stopped him, saying: 'In the Jianwu era our family all received glory and favor—one clan, five marquises.
units.literal: Later his younger brother Wei sought for his son Shang the Princess Jingxiang, daughter of Prince Ying of Chu; Tiao heard of it and stopped him, saying: 'In the Jianwu era our family all received glory and favor—one clan, five marquises.

units.zh: 時特進一言，女可以配王，男可以尚主，但以貴寵過盛，即為禍患，故不為也。
units.en: At that time an eminence grandee needed but one word and daughters could marry princes and sons could marry princesses—but because excessive honor becomes calamity, I did not do so.
units.literal: At that time an eminence grandee needed but one word and daughters could marry princes and sons could marry princesses—but because excessive honor becomes calamity, I did not do so.

units.zh: 且爾一子，奈何棄之於楚乎？』
units.en: Moreover you have but one son—how can you cast him off to Chu?'
units.literal: Moreover you have but one son—how can you cast him off to Chu?'

units.zh: 其後廣陵王荊有罪，帝以至親悼傷之，詔鯈與羽林監南陽任隗雜理其獄。
units.en: Later Prince Liu Jing of Guangling committed crimes; grieving as close kin, the emperor ordered Fan Tiao and the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Ren Wei of Nanyang to jointly try the case.
units.literal: Later Prince Jing of Guangling committed crimes; the emperor, grieving as close kin, ordered Tiao and the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Ren Wei of Nanyang to jointly try the case.

units.zh: 事竟，奏請誅荊。
units.en: When the case was concluded, they memorialized requesting Jing's execution.
units.literal: When the affair was concluded, they memorialized requesting Jing's execution.

units.zh: 及沛王輔事發，貴戚子弟多見收捕，鯈以不豫得免。
units.en: When Prince Liu Fu of Pei fell, many imperial in-laws were arrested; Fan Tiao escaped because he had never joined their circle.
units.literal: When the Prince of Pei Fu affair broke, noble affines' sons and younger kin were mostly seized and arrested; Tiao because he had not participated obtained exemption.

units.zh: 鯈益以此知名。
units.en: Fan Tiao became even more renowned for this.
units.literal: Tiao became even more famed for this.

units.zh: 鄉部吏司因此為奸，鯈常疾之。
units.en: Rural officials turned the mess to their profit; Fan Tiao despised it.
units.literal: Village department clerks for this reason practiced villainy; Tiao always hated it.

units.zh: 鯈並欲奏罷之，疾病未及得上。
units.en: Fan Tiao meant to abolish both practices but fell ill before he could memorialize.
units.literal: Tiao also wished to memorialize to abolish them; illness came before he could submit upward.

units.zh: 音歸，具以聞，帝覽之而悲嘆，敕二郡並令從之。
units.en: Zhang Yin reported everything; the emperor read Fan Tiao's words with grief and ordered both commanderies to comply.
units.literal: Yin returned, reported it all in full; the emperor read it and sighed in grief, ordered the two commanderies together to order compliance with it.

units.zh: 其後楚事發覺，帝追念鯈謹恪，又聞其止鮪婚事，故其諸子得不坐焉。
units.en: When the Chu conspiracy broke, the emperor remembered Fan Tiao's caution and his refusal of Fan Wei's marriage scheme, and spared his sons.
units.literal: Later when the Chu affair was discovered, the emperor recalled Tiao's careful reverence, and also heard that he had stopped Wei's marriage affair; therefore his various sons were able not to be implicated.
